---
title: "Performance and platforms"
description: "How fast zupmxode compiles and solves against rxode2 and mrgsolve, and which tier runs where."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This page is for readers who want to know what zupmxode costs before they
use it: how its compile and solve times compare with rxode2 and mrgsolve
on the same machine, and where it runs native code or MIR's interpreter.

## Benchmarks

`tools/run-benchmarks` in the source repository times each workload of
the package's design (§10) for every engine installed, and keeps every run
in `.agents/benchmarks.csv`. The table shows the latest measured run of
each row. "zupmxode/lsoda" is zupmxode made to use LSODA, rxode2's
solver, where it would choose the matrix exponential.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
csv <- file.path("..", "..", ".agents", "benchmarks.csv")
b <- utils::read.csv(csv)
b <- b[!is.na(b$value), ]
b <- b[!duplicated(b[c("row", "engine")], fromLast = TRUE), ]
rows <- c(compile_2cpt = "Compile a two-compartment model",
          candidates_200 = "200 candidate models, compiled and run",
          closed_form_1e6 = "Closed form, 1e6 subjects",
          ode_2cpt_1thread = "Two-compartment ODE, 1e3 x 1e3, 1 thread",
          ode_2cpt_interp = "The same, interpreter tier",
          ejcp_obs_per_s = "Seven-cycle antibody workload, obs/s")
targets <- c(compile_2cpt = "under 20 ms", candidates_200 = "faster than rxode2",
             closed_form_1e6 = "matches rxode2", ode_2cpt_1thread = "within 1.5x of rxode2",
             ode_2cpt_interp = "recorded", ejcp_obs_per_s = "above 5,000")
b <- b[b$row %in% names(rows), ]
wide <- stats::reshape(b[c("row", "engine", "value")], idvar = "row", timevar = "engine",
                       direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^value\\.", "", names(wide))
wide <- wide[match(names(rows), wide$row), ]
engines <- intersect(c("zupmxode", "zupmxode/lsoda", "rxode2", "mrgsolve"), names(wide))
out <- data.frame(Workload = rows[wide$row], Target = targets[wide$row],
                  wide[engines], check.names = FALSE)
# Each value on its own, three significant digits, never scientific.
fmt <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "fg", digits = 3, big.mark = ","))
out[engines] <- lapply(out[engines], fmt)
knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE)
```

Times are in seconds, except the last row. They were taken on one
`r b$machine[1]`, a machine that was not idle; rxode2's closed-form row is
from an earlier day, when it had the memory that row needs. That build of
R has no OpenMP, so every row ran on one thread. The two-compartment ODE
misses its target (issue
[#34](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zupmxode/issues/34)); the compile and
candidate rows, which a model-building loop pays for, are two orders of
magnitude ahead.

## Tiers

zupmxode runs a model on one of two **tiers**: native code generated by
MIR, or MIR's interpreter. Both give the same doubles, which the test
suite checks on every model. The interpreter is the fallback where native
code cannot be made; in the table above it is about 1.4 times slower with
the matrix exponential and 1.6 times with LSODA. `pmx_ode_info()` names a
model's tier and `pmx_ode_tier()` changes it.

Both tiers run on every leg of the package's R CMD check, which a test
asserts on each of them:

| Leg | Tiers |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, R-release | native and interpreter |
| Windows, R-release and R-devel | native and interpreter |
| Ubuntu, R-release and R-oldrel | native and interpreter |
| Linux containers, R-devel (clang 23 and the other compilers R CMD check runs on) | native and interpreter |

Both tiers need memory that is writable and executable. Where the system
refuses it (SELinux's `deny_execmem`, some hardened containers), neither
runs and models cannot be solved; `zumir::zumir_info()` says why. On
macOS, R needs the `allow-jit` entitlement that CRAN's build of R has.
